title: Dexketoprofen Plus Paracetamol for Pain After Lower Wisdom Tooth Removal
official: Combination of Dexketoprofen and Paracetamol for the Treatment of Acute Pain After Surgical Extraction of Mandibular Third Molars: A Randomized Clinical Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether taking dexketoprofen and paracetamol together every 8 hours controls pain as well as the usual regimen of alternating dexketoprofen and paracetamol every 4 hours in adults after surgical removal of lower wisdom teeth. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the combined regimen (dexketoprofen 25 mg plus paracetamol 650 mg every 8 hours) provide pain control similar to or better than the alternating regimen (dexketoprofen 25 mg and paracetamol 1000 mg alternated every 4 hours)?
* Do the two regimens differ in the need for rescue pain medication, side effects, patient satisfaction and quality of life during the first days after surgery?

Researchers will compare the two pain medication regimens. All participants will receive active pain treatment and will have access to rescue medication if needed.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two regimens, without knowing which one they receive
* Have their lower wisdom tooth removed at the CEU Cardenal Herrera University Dental Clinic
* Take the study capsules for 5 days after surgery
* Record their pain level, any rescue medication and side effects in a diary during the 5 days after surgery
* Complete short questionnaires on anxiety before surgery and on recovery and satisfaction after surgery
* Return for suture removal 7 days after surgery
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 to 65 years
* Indication for surgical extraction of a mandibular third molar due to pathology or orthodontic reasons
* ASA physical status I or II
* Signed informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Allergy or hypersensitivity to paracetamol, dexketoprofen or other NSAIDs
* Hypersensitivity to metamizole or other pyrazolones
* History of agranulocytosis or other blood dyscrasias
* ASA physical status III or higher
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Use of medication that may interfere with the effects of the study drugs during the week before surgery
* Inability to attend the follow-up visit (e.g., non-resident or floating population)
